text:
rina: hi all, newbie question — trying to spin up `docker-compose up` on my M1 laptop. postgres container crashes on first run with `initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied`. I mounted a local folder `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` because I want DB files on disk. any quick tips?

sam: welcome! :wave: mac + bind mounts are harsh. two simple options: switch to a named volume (recommended), or make the host folder owned by the postgres UID inside the container.

rina: how do I do the chown-from-container trick? sudo chown on host didn't seem to stick with Docker Desktop.

dev-ops: run this from the repo root: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /data"`. The container runs as root and updates the host-mounted dir in a way Docker Desktop accepts.

sam: also set permissions: `chmod 700 ./pgdata`. Postgres initdb insists on strict perms.

rina: thanks — is 999 always the right UID?

dev-ops: official postgres images use 999 usually, but if you're pinning an image or using variants, check with: `docker run --rm postgres:15 id -u postgres` to verify.

rina: got it. If I don't care about files on host, how to use named volume in compose quickly?

sam: change your compose like:

```
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pass
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

That avoids host FS weirdness on mac.

rina: weirdly, after switching to named volume, initdb still failed once with a message about invalid system time while creating base dir 😕

dev-ops: hmm, did you force `platform: linux/amd64` anywhere? On M1 emulation can cause subtle failures. Also check Docker Desktop > Resources > File Sharing and disable gRPC FUSE temporarily if you're running into strange mount semantics.

rina: I didn't set platform. I will try disabling gRPC FUSE.

deploy-bot: note: local onboarding recommends `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` env in compose and using a named volume for mac. See onboarding link in #new-hires.

sam: one more gotcha: if you have both redis and postgres volumes, docker-compose sometimes reuses names from previous runs. Use `docker-compose down -v` to tear down volumes and start fresh when testing mount changes.

rina: sweet, `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /data"` + chmod + named volume path change fixed it. DB came up and migrations ran. thanks folks! :tada:

dev-ops: great — ping us if migrations hang. sometimes local CI credentials (PGUSER/PGPASSWORD) can differ from compose env and cause waiting loops during startup scripts.

rina: noted. appreciate the help :)
